advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the per-candidate canonicalization in _is_ambiguous_snapshot_candidate (or the scan loop) so one malformed row defers that key instead of aborting the diff phase.
evidence: run_differs.py:261 `refresh_scoped_snapshot(ctx)` — called with no surrounding try/except
Old code no-oped for unscoped passes: diff shows removed `if not scoped_ids: return`
The scoped path tolerates only transport errors via `_safe_get_issue`; the new canonicalization step has no equivalent guard
advisory.finding: The new unscoped candidate scan calls inbound_mapper.map_remote_to_local() on every ambiguous-prefilter hit with no exception handling, and refresh_scoped_snapshot is invoked unguarded at run_differs.py:261. A malformed snapshot/baseline row that makes the mapper raise now aborts the entire diff phase, whereas an unscoped pass was previously a guaranteed no-op (the old `if not scoped_ids: return`). This is a behavior/regression risk broadening the blast radius of a single bad row.
scenarios: An unscoped production pass encounters one binding whose raw baseline or snapshot entry has an unexpected shape the mapper cannot handle
A mapper implementation that raises on a missing/odd field

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish 'mapper unresolved' from 'no ambiguous candidates' — log/raise when the mapper cannot be obtained on a pass that has candidate rows, rather than returning an empty list.
evidence: snapshot_lagfree_refresh.py:190 `except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — partial test ctx: no mapper means safe no-op`
snapshot_lagfree_refresh.py:155-156 `if get_baseline is None or inbound_mapper is None: return []`
The empty-list result is later indistinguishable at the call site: refresh_scoped_snapshot only checks `if jira_keys:`
advisory.finding: _inbound_mapper_for returns None on ANY exception (and when runtime_backend/inbound is absent), and _unscoped_ambiguous_jira_keys then returns [] — silently skipping the entire unscoped clobber-protection. The verdict 'no ambiguous keys to refresh' is indistinguishable from 'the mapper could not be resolved', so a failed mapper resolution fails open: the protective refresh never runs and nothing signals it.
scenarios: A production unscoped pass where runtime_backend is set but backend.inbound is None and the fallback select_backend(compose_config()) raises for a real configuration reason

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide the correct default when binding_store has no is_pending (treat as skip/unknown) rather than silently defaulting to 'not pending'.
evidence: snapshot_lagfree_refresh.py:195-196 `is_pending = getattr(binding_store, "is_pending", None)` / `return bool(is_pending(local_id)) if is_pending is not None else False`
Real BindingStore.is_pending exists (binding_store.py:207), so the fallback branch only fires for a store that cannot answer the pending question
advisory.finding: _is_pending_binding returns False whenever the binding_store lacks an is_pending method, so a store without that method is treated as if every binding is confirmed. The pending-exclusion guard fails open: an absent capability is silently read as 'not pending' rather than as an inability to check.
scenarios: A binding_store duck-type (or future/refactored store) without is_pending — pending bindings would be treated as confirmed arbitration candidates

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Remove the unused all_bindings() test helper or wire the production scan/tests to the source it actually uses.
evidence: Production scan source is `for local_ticket in getattr(ctx, "local_tickets", None) or []` (snapshot_lagfree_refresh.py:158)
No reference to all_bindings in snapshot_lagfree_refresh.py
advisory.finding: The test store adds an all_bindings() method (test file, _CtxBindingStore) but no production code path consumes it in this change; _unscoped_ambiguous_jira_keys iterates ctx.local_tickets instead. The added test helper is dead relative to the code under test and may mislead future readers into thinking the scan is driven by all_bindings.
scenarios: Future maintenance assuming the candidate scan is binding-driven

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an unscoped test where a local ticket carries only `id` (no `ticket_id`) and assert its ambiguous key is refreshed.
evidence: tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_scoped_snapshot_overlay_f449.py:388 anonymous = _local(...); anonymous.pop("ticket_id") — no `id` key is set, so `.get("id")` also returns None; the `id` fallback branch is never taken with a present value
Named violating input: local_tickets=[{"id": "loc-1", "description": "NEW body", ...}] (no ticket_id) should still resolve to a refresh candidate but no test confirms it
advisory.finding: The `local_id = local_ticket.get("ticket_id") or local_ticket.get("id")` identity fallback (newly added) is never positively exercised: no test supplies a local ticket keyed only on `id` (no `ticket_id`). The one no-identity test pops `ticket_id` and adds no `id`, so it exercises only the None path. Dropping the `or local_ticket.get("id")` clause would not fail any test.
